page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-12 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the GPU Machines family. The instance is powered by an x86_64 architecture featuring 12 dedicated vCPUs and 45.0 GB of system memory, providing an average memory allocation of 3.75 GB per virtual core. It integrates hardware acceleration through a partitioned 0.25 share of an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU based on the Blackwell architecture, supplying 24 GB of total video RAM to the instance.

Storage architecture relies entirely on external network-attached volumes, as the instance includes no local storage. Networking provisions do not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated network address translation or allocated external IPs for direct public ingress and egress. By offering a fractional GPU slice, the server provides cost-efficient access to modern workstation-grade graphics hardware without requiring the expense of a dedicated full GPU.

The combination of 12 dedicated vCPUs, 45 GB of RAM, and partitioned RTX PRO 6000 graphics acceleration suits workloads requiring dedicated compute paired with moderate visualization or inference capability. Primary target workloads include remote virtual workstations, computer-aided design (CAD) processing, 3D graphics rendering pipelines, streaming video encoding, and entry-level machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-12 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for graphics and visualization workloads. Based on the x86_64 processor architecture, it provides 12 dedicated vCPUs paired with 45.0 GB of system RAM, resulting in approximately 3.75 GB of memory per core. Compute resources are coupled with a fractional 0.25 allocation of an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPU providing 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance does not include local disk storage, depending instead on network storage volumes, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The fractional GPU partition offers an economical approach to running graphics acceleration, bypassing the cost barrier of provisioning an entire physical accelerator. The g4-standard-12 is appropriately configured for cloud-hosted virtual desktops, 3D graphics rendering, video transcode pipelines, and lightweight model inference tasks requiring dedicated processing cores and professional-grade graphics hardware.
